newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders eye EU wheat subsidy of 8-10 Ecus/tonne.
newsitem.headline: Traders eye EU wheat subsidy of 8-10 Ecus/tonne.

text.p: Several European grain exporters said they expected the European Union to grant a rebate of between eight and 10 Ecus per tonne for wheat at its weekly grain tender later on Thursday.
That would add up to a subtantial drop in volume from last week's exports of 477,700 tonnes, with traders generally predicting a volume closer to 200,000 tonnes this time.

An estimate for the breakdown of Thursday's bids through France shows the predicted range of eight to 10 Ecus would involve the release of betweeen 120,000 and 295,000 tonnes of soft wheat, plus whatever came through from other member states.
Some traders were confident, however, that the EU would grant up to 400,000 tonnes, which would imply a refund closer to 12 Ecus.
Exporters bidding through France asked to export 725,550 tonnes of EU soft wheat at rebates ranging from 7.49 to 17.44 Ecus per tonne.
Traders stressed it was difficult to predict the level of refund, especially after a recent export warning by the European Commission's director general for agriculture, Guy Legras.
"Much will hinge on the goodwill of the Commission in Brussels," one exporter said.
Last Friday Legras warned that the EU may slow down exports, having already shipped more than one million tonnes of wheat over the last two weeks.
Legras' warning dampened traders' hopes of grabbing substantial export licences in the last grain auction for 1996.
"We are completely tied up," one said.
A majority of exporters believed that two operators were behind the first three rebate offers placed in France.
These offers ranging from 7.49 Ecus to 9.42 Ecus involved the export of up to 200,000 tonnes of wheat.
